JUDGMENT

The Police Inspector of Parappana Agrahara Police Station submitted charge sheet against accused for the offences punishable under Section 498(A), 506 of Indian Penal Code and Section 3, 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
2. Prosecution Case: On 21-06-2019, at the time of engagement of Smt Namitha with the accused CW4 Sri Janardhan gave 7 grams gold ring, Rs.15,000/- for clothes to accused and spent KABC030181372021 CC No.6076/2021 Rs.1,50,000/- for betrothal ceremony.
In October 2019, the accused received Rs.5 lakhs from CW4 and Rs.5 lakhs from CW10 Harshitha through RTGS towards purchase of flat.

Thereafter, on 18-11-2019 the marriage of CW1 and the accused was solemnized and they were living in house bearing No.7, 2 nd Floor, situated at Silicon Town,
Doddanagamangala Village, Begur Hobli, Electronic City Post, within the limits of Parappana Agrahara Police Station.

Later the accused started ill-treating CW1 by not providing food and basic amenities and harassing her to fetch dowry from her parental house to purchase flat and subjected her to mental and physical cruelty and thereby committed the alleged offences.
3. First Information Report:

On the basis of first information given by informant cum CW1 namely Smt.Namitha, CW11 Sri Nagaraj Havanoor, PSI of Parappanaha Agrahara Police Station registered Crime No.08/2021 against the accused for the offenses punishable under Section 498(A), 504 of IPC and Section 3, 4 of D. P. Act, prepared FIR and sent the same to the Court and to his superior officers.
4. Investigation: CW11 after registration of case, has conducted spot mahazar as per Ex.P2 and handed over the case papers to CW12 namely Sri Sandeep S .
CW12 on the receipt of case papers has KABC030181372021 CC No.6076/2021 proceeded with further investigation by collecting the necessary documents and recorded the statement of requisite witnesses.

After completion of investigation, the I.O/ CW12 has submitted charge sheet against accused for the offenses punishable under Section 498(A), 504 of IPC and Section 3, 4 of D. P. Act.
5.
The accused was enlarged on bail at the pre- summoning or crime stage by the order dated 31-3- 2021 .

6. On receipt of charge sheet, this Court took cognizance of offences alleged against the accused No.1 and 2.
7.
Copies of prosecution papers as required U/Sec.207 of Cr.P.C have been furnished to the accused.
8. Charge:

After hearing learned Sr.APP and counsel for accused, charge for the offences punishable Smt. Namita vs Jayanta Gowda on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72456557/
2 U/Sec.498(A), 506 of Indian Penal Code and Section 3, 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act has been framed,
read over and explained to the accused in the language known to him, who, in turn, pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
KABC030181372021 CC No.6076/2021 9. Prosecution Evidence:
The prosecution in order to establish its case cited 12 witnesses however examined two witnesses and exhibited 4 documents.

The learned Sr. APP prayed for issuance of witness summons to other witnesses however his prayer was rejected on the ground that no purpose would be served, since the material witnesses have not supported the case and the side of prosecution was taken as closed by the order dated 24-09-2024.

10. Accused statement as per section 313 of CrPC: There are no incriminating evidences against the accused from the evidence of prosecution thereby the recording of statement of accused as per Sec.313 of Cr.P.C. is dispensed with.
11. Heard the arguments.
Perused materials on the record.

12. The following point are arises for consideration is as follows;
1.

Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that the marriage of CW1 Smt.
Namitha was solemnized with accused on 18-11-2019 KABC030181372021 CC No.6076/2021 and the couple were residing in No.7, 2nd Floor, Silicon Town, Doddanagamangala Village, Begur Hobli,
Electronic City Post, within the limits of Parappana Agrahaa PS, at that time , the accused subjected her to mental and physical cruelty thereby resulted in commission of the offences punishable under Sec.498(A) of IPC?

2. Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that the accused had threatened her with criminal intimidation thereby resulted in commission of the offences punishable under Sec.506 of IPC?

3. Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that after engagement, the accused received Rs.5 lakhs from CW4 Sri Janardhan and Rs.5 lakhs from CW10 KABC030181372021 CC No.6076/2021 Harshitha and at the time of marriage the accused received 15 grams of chain as dowry from CW4 thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable u/Sec.3 of Dowry Prohibition Act?

4. Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that after the marriage accused started harassing CW1 to bring dowry from her parental house for purchase of flat in his name thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable u/Sec.4 of Dowry Prohibition Act?
5. What order?

13. My findings on the above points are as under:
Smt. Namita vs Jayanta Gowda on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72456557/
3  Point No.1-4 : In the Negative  Point No.5 : As per final order  KABC030181372021 CC No.6076/2021  REASONS 14. Point No.1 to 4: These points are taken up together for the purpose of common discussion in order to avoid repetition of facts as they form the same part of transaction.

In support of prosecution case as narrated in paragraph 2 and the point for consideration in paragraph 12 of this judgment, the prosecution examined the witnesses which are as follows i. CW1 by name Smt.Namitha, being Informant examined as PW1 deposed that she has identified her signatures on Ex.P1 (complaint) and Ex.P2 (spot mahazar).

When she went to police station for sorting out minor differences of opinion among-st her and accused, the police obtained her signatures on the said documents and she pleaded ignorance about the contents of complaint and spot mahazar.
In this regard, the learned Sr.APP has cross examined her by treating her as hostile witness however no favorable answer has been elicited from her mouth to support the prosecution case.

Her denial of statement given before the police is marked as Ex.P3.
KABC030181372021 CC No.6076/2021 ii. CW4 Sri Janardhan examined as PW2 deposed that CW1 is his daughter, he knew accused, CW2, 3 and CW6 to CW9, CW5 is his wife, CW10 his second daughter.
He denied the complaint given by her daughter in respect of cruelty and dowry harassment between CW1 and accused.
In this regard, the learned Sr.APP has cross examined this witness by treating him as hostile witness however no favorable answer has been elicited from his mouth to support the prosecution case.

His denial of statement given before the police is marked as Ex.P4.
14.
PW1 is the informant cum victim and PW2 is her father
have not supported the prosecution case.
The learned Sr.APP prays for issuance of summons to other witnesses.
It is seen from the entire records that, PW.1 and PW2 are material witnesses to the prosecution case however they did not support the prosecution case in any manner.
Under these circumstances, this court is of the opinion that, even if other witness examined by the prosecution and they supported the prosecution that would not helpful to the case of prosecution.
At this background, this court feels it is a waste of precious time of Court in examining other witness.
Moreover the evidence of other witnesses is only formal in nature.

Therefore, the prayer of learned Sr.APP is KABC030181372021 CC No.6076/2021 rejected and the prosecution evidence is taken as closed by the order dated 24/09/2024.
15.
It is seen from the deposition of PW1 and PW2 that the disputes between the accused No. 1 and the PW1 have been settled.

But the learned APP argued that the Section 498A R/w Section 34 of Smt. Namita vs Jayanta Gowda on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72456557/
4

Indian Penal code is not compoundable case as per section 320 of CR.P.C. and hence the examination of witnesses is necessary but this court dispensed the same on account of amicable settlement arrived between the rival parties to the case.
Yes this court agrees with the view of the learned Sr.APP that the section 498A of IPC is not compoundable and the same cannot be compounded as per Section 320 of CR.P.C.

This court places reliance in the case of B.S. JOSHI AND ORS. V. STATE OF HARYANA AND ANR IN THE MATTER OF AIR 2003 SCW 1824, wherein it was held that, "in a case where matrimonial disputes have been resolved between the parties then in that case offence under Section 498A of I.P.C. may be compounded between the parties for according to them an opportunity to settle in life afresh.

entities.text: B.S. JOSHI AND ORS. V. STATE OF HARYANA AND ANR
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
. This court further places reliance upon the decision in the case of Ranjana Banerjee v. Bijay Bhushan Banerjee and Ors., 1996(2) East. Cri. C. 808 (Pat), wherein this lordship observed which runs thus:
"It appears that good sense have been prevailed amongst the spouses and when it became impossible for them to lead conjugal life any further and when the matrimonial home has been broken for all practical purposes, they have decided to withdraw all allegations and counter allegations against each other and get themselves separated on divorce by mutual consent.

entities.text: Ranjana Banerjee v. Bijay Bhushan Banerjee and Ors., 1996(2) East. Cri. C. 808 (Pat)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Although, Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code is not compoundable, but in the nature and circumstances of the case and the situation prevailing, accord is hereby granted to compromise the dispute between the parties and hence joint petition filed in both the cases are hereby allowed."

It further held that after examining the nature of the case and the circumstances, under which the offence has been committed, it would be proper to compound the offence and in my opinion, it would be also meet the ends of justice."
KABC030181372021 CC No.6076/2021 17.
ADMITTEDLY, the disputes between the PW1 and accused have been resolved.
The criminal case under Section 498A of I.P.C. is the off-shoot of the said matrimonial dispute.
The parties have come to their terms and in pursuance thereto the CW1/Pw1 does not intend to proceed with this case and hence she has not supported the prosecution case.

18. In the matter of the KRISHNA vs STATE OF KARNATAKA reported in Laws (Kar) 2014 4 464,
wherein it was held that "it would be unfair or contrary to the interest of justice to continue with the criminal proceeding or continuation of criminal proceeding would tantamount to abuse of process of law despite settlement and compromise between the victim and the wrongdoer and whether to secure the ends of justice, it is appropriate that criminal case is put to an end".
Smt. Namita vs Jayanta Gowda on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72456557/
5 19.

entities.text: KRISHNA vs STATE OF KARNATAKA reported in Laws (Kar) 2014 4 464
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Under these circumstances and on account of the preposition laid down by the Hon'ble Apex and Hon'ble High Court, even if other witnesses examined by the prosecution, they did supported the prosecution, would not helpful to the prosecution.
In this background, this court feels it is a waste of precious time of the Court in examining other witnesses.
Moreover the evidence of other witnesses is only formal in nature.

Therefore, the prayer of learned KABC030181372021 CC No.6076/2021 Sr.APP is rejected and prosecution evidence is taken as closed and hence the offence under section 498A of IPC with other offences under section 324, 504, 506 of IPC cannot be proved beyond reasonable doubt.
Accordingly, this court answers the point No.1 to 4 in the Negative.

20. Point No.5:- In view of the above findings and reasons given on point No.1 to 4, this Court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER Acting U/Sec.248(1) of the Cr.P.C.
(i) The accused is found not guilty and acquitted from the offences punishable under Sec.498(A), 506 of Indian Penal Code and Section 3, 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
(ii) Accused is set at liberty.
(iii) In view of Section 437-A of Cr.P.C his bail bond shall be in force for 6 (six) months.
KABC030181372021 CC No.6076/2021 (iv) Ordered accordingly.

Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru City.
